t: Juche holds that the masses of the people are the masters of the revolution and that a country prospers once it achieves political, economic and military self-reliance, which North Korea's government pursued from the 1950s.

In the famine of 1994 to 1999 estimates of the dead range from 240,000 to 3,500,000, and the UN commission of inquiry of 2014 found violations by the state, including prison camps and executions, that the government rejects.

Scholars disagree about what Juche is: Brian Reynolds Myers likens it to Japanese fascism and ultranationalism, Charles K. Armstrong calls it a quasi-religion, and Derek R. Ford stresses its continuity with Marxism–Leninism.
dyk: Juche was a word of German philosophy before it was a doctrine: it was coined in Japan in 1887 to translate Subjekt, and North Korean editions of Marx used it even before 1955. The Juche calendar counts years from 1912, the year of Kim Il Sung's birth.
ev: Kim Il Sung gives the “Juche speech”, the first documented reference to Juche as an ideology
A failed challenge to Kim Il Sung's leadership leads to a purge of pro-Soviet and pro-Chinese elements from the Workers' Party of Korea
Kim Jong Il introduces Kimilsungism and the Ten Principles for the Establishment of a Monolithic Ideological System
On the Juche Idea is published under Kim Jong Il's name
Kim Jong Il introduces Socialism of Our Style after the revolutions that brought down the Eastern Bloc
The North Korean famine, called the Arduous March by the government, causes mass starvation; estimates of deaths range from 240,000 to 3,500,000
The Juche calendar is adopted, counting years from 1912
A UN commission of inquiry publishes a 400-page report on human rights in North Korea; the government rejects its findings

f.thinkers: Kim Il Sung, to whom North Korean sources attribute it; Hwang Jang-yop, his top adviser on philosophy, whom Western scholars generally credit with its conceptualisation and early development; Kim Jong Il, who declared it a distinct ideology in the 1970s and developed it further; Kim Jong Un, who succeeded him
f.texts: Kim Il Sung's speech “On Eliminating Dogmatism and Formalism and Establishing Juche in Ideological Work” (1955), the “Juche speech”; his 1967 speech to the Supreme People's Assembly on independence, self-sustenance and self-defence; the Ten Principles for the Establishment of a Monolithic Ideological System (1974); Kim Jong Il's On the Juche Idea (1982)
f.ideas: the masses of the people as the masters of the revolution and its motive force; political independence (chaju); economic self-sufficiency (charip); military self-reliance (chawi); the primacy of ideology and political consciousness; the leader at the centre of the masses (suryong); opposition to reliance on great powers (sadae)
f.today: It is the official ideology of North Korea and the Workers' Party of Korea, in the form of Kimilsungism–Kimjongilism until the party's 9th Congress in 2026 removed that name from its rules; abroad it has been adopted or studied by small parties and groups, such as the Nepal Workers' and Peasants' Party
